Save a ggplot at HVTI manuscript defaults

Source: R/save-manuscript.R
save_manuscript.Rd

A thin wrapper around ggplot2::ggsave() that enforces the house manuscript figure size, 6 inches wide by 4 inches tall, so journal figures come out at a consistent size in one call. It is the manuscript counterpart of save_ppt(), which enforces the slide panel box.

Usage

save_manuscript(
  plot,
  file,
  width = 6,
  height = 4,
  units = "in",
  device = NULL,
  dpi = 300,
  draft_file = NULL,
  draft_dpi = NULL,
  format = c("tiff", "png"),
  footnote = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

plot

A ggplot2::ggplot() object, e.g. plot(hv_*()) finished with theme_hv_manuscript().

file

Output file path. Its extension sets the format (.pdf, .tiff, .png, ...). Without an extension, format supplies one.

width, height, units

Figure size. Default 6 x 4 "in", the HVTI manuscript default.

device

Graphics device. NULL (default) lets ggplot2 pick from the file extension, and a TIFF is written LZW-compressed by ragg::agg_tiff(). When you pass a device, file is used as given and format adds no extension. For font embedding in a PDF, pass grDevices::cairo_pdf (requires cairo/X11 support).

dpi

Resolution for raster formats. Default 300.

draft_file

Optional second output file path (typically .png). When supplied, an additional raster copy of plot is written here at the same width/height/units, for dragging into a Word draft manuscript. Default NULL (no draft copy written).

draft_dpi

Resolution for draft_file. Default NULL, which falls back to dpi.

format

Raster format, "tiff" (default) or "png", for a file or draft_file given without an extension. A path that has an extension keeps it. Passing a format that contradicts a raster extension, such as format = "png" with a .tiff path, is an error.

footnote

Optional provenance note, NULL (default) for none. A character vector of fields, which are joined by a middle dot (U+00B7) with a space either side, or a single string, which is split into fields at that separator. Fields may not contain line breaks. With NULL, the output is exactly what it is without the argument. R's pdf() device draws only Latin-1 text and warns on anything else; use device = grDevices::cairo_pdf for a note in another script.

...

Further arguments passed to ggplot2::ggsave() for the primary file. Not applied to draft_file.

Value

Invisibly, the file path, with the extension format added when it had none. With a footnote, the path carries the attribute "dims", a list of the saved width, height and units of file, after any scale passed in ..., the height including the strip, and, when draft_file is written, "draft_dims" for that file.

Details

Pair it with theme_hv_manuscript(), whose 12 pt base_size supplies the manuscript typography. Like save_ppt(), save_manuscript() fixes the output geometry, not the theme; style the plot first, then save.

The device is inferred from the file extension by default. A .tif or .tiff file is written as an LZW-compressed TIFF at dpi, so a 6 x 4 in figure is 1800 x 1200 pixels, the same geometry as the PNG, without the tens of megabytes an uncompressed TIFF takes. A path with no extension takes one from format, which defaults to "tiff", the raster format journals ask for. An extension you write is never overridden, so a .png path, such as one a Quarto or R Markdown report embeds, stays a PNG: browsers do not display TIFF.

For a .pdf where you want fonts embedded (so 12 pt type renders exactly as designed), pass device = grDevices::cairo_pdf (on a system with cairo/X11 support).

Publisher-accepted formats, vector (PDF, EPS) or TIFF (a raster format also accepted by journals), often produce large or fragile files when dragged into a Word manuscript. Word has no native PDF-as-picture support and silently converts them to bloated, sometimes unreadable EMF. Pass draft_file (typically a .png path) to also write a small raster copy alongside file in the same call: keep file as the publisher deliverable submitted to the journal, and drag draft_file into the Word draft instead.

Pass footnote to print the figure's provenance, typically the fields provenance_footnote() builds, in a strip reserved below the plot. The strip is added to the figure, never drawn over it: the plot keeps its width x height and the saved file is taller by the strip. The note is measured with each output device's own font metrics, so a PDF, PNG and TIFF of one figure may get strips of slightly different height. It is set at 8 pt and shrinks to fit one line, down to a floor of 6 pt. Past the floor it wraps: first between fields, so a field that fits on a line, the commit ID among them, is never broken; then inside a field too wide for a line, at /, . and spaces, so a long job path breaks at its directory and name parts. Nothing is clipped or truncated; the strip grows to as many lines as the note needs. The saved height is rounded up to a whole pixel (raster) or point (PDF), so the reported height is the height written. The note goes on publication figures too: a journal crops it in typesetting, and the study's copy keeps the record of which version of the job drew it.

See also

provenance_footnote() to build the footnote fields, save_ppt() for slides, theme_hv_manuscript() for the 12 pt typography, hv_ggsave_dims() for fixed-panel sizing. Worked examples live in the HVTI ggplot graphics recipes book, https://ehrlinger.github.io/hvtiGraphics/.

Examples

# \donttest{
p <- plot(hv_survival(sample_survival_data(n = 200, seed = 42))) +
  theme_hv_manuscript()
save_manuscript(p, file.path(tempdir(), "survival.pdf"))

# no extension: a 300 dpi, LZW-compressed survival.tiff
save_manuscript(p, file.path(tempdir(), "survival"))

# the same figure as a PNG
save_manuscript(p, file.path(tempdir(), "survival"), format = "png")

# also write a small draft PNG for dragging into Word
save_manuscript(p, file.path(tempdir(), "survival.pdf"),
                 draft_file = file.path(tempdir(), "survival_draft.png"))

# print the render's provenance in a strip below the figure
out <- save_manuscript(
  p, file.path(tempdir(), "survival.pdf"),
  footnote = provenance_footnote(
    commit = "3f9c2a1", job = "30_analyses/survival.qmd",
    time = as.POSIXct("2026-10-29 14:40")
  )
)
attr(out, "dims")
#> $width
#> [1] 6
#> 
#> $height
#> [1] 4.291667
#> 
#> $units
#> [1] "in"
#> 
# }
